findings.location: _score_result(): declared quality checks are loaded but never evaluated; scoring collapses to generic checks
findings.line: eval_runner.py:85 (quality_checks: list[str] = task.get("quality_checks", [])  # noqa: F841 - the only reference to quality_checks in the entire backend/ tree); executed checks only at 92-139; tasks.json quality_checks blocks (eval_001 lines 10-14 ... eval_011 lines 124-127); eval_006-eval_011 have expected_fields=[]
findings.finding: _score_result() loads each task's quality_checks into a local variable and immediately abandons it (explicit # noqa: F841, only reference in the codebase). No declared quality criterion is ever enforced - e.g. 'findings should reference real files under backend/app/api/' or 'diagnosis should identify the missing None check'. For eval_006...eval_011 (expected_fields=[]), scoring therefore reduces to three generic checks: status != blocked, summary longer than ~10 chars, and the verified flag. The suite's scores (and the slow tests' >=0.5/0.6 pass thresholds) overstate conformance to tasks.json's own contract, and the expected_fields check itself is plain substring containment in the serialized JSON, so a field name appearing anywhere passes. No unit test exercises _score_result at all (fast tests only validate file shape and registry wiring).
findings.evidence: Read of eval_runner.py in full (line 85 with noqa F841; checks executed: status 93-98, summary 100-105, verified 107-114, expected_fields substring 116-123, story count 125-139); grep 'quality_checks' over backend/ -> only eval_runner.py:85; tasks.json quality_checks present on eval_001-eval_005 and eval_006-eval_011 (the latter with empty expected_fields); pytest run: tests/evals/test_evals.py fast tests all PASSED while no test asserts quality-check execution.
findings.production_impact: Evaluation-validity defect, not a runtime defect: the eval score is a weaker measurement than its own definition claims, so the suite can green-light agents whose outputs miss the documented quality bar. No production behavior is affected today (the suite is not a deploy gate and never runs in CI).
findings.confidence: High (full file read + repo-wide grep + live test run)
findings.recommendation: Implement the declared checks as JSON-aware per-task predicates (or rename/strip the field so the tasks file stops promising measurements that never run); add a fast unit test covering _score_result itself.

findings.location: compare_to_baseline()/run_benchmark(): a zero-run current window resolves to all-benign (perfect 1.0) objectives, so the gate fails open on a cold process
findings.line: benchmark_manager.py:172-181 (_latency_score None -> 1.0), 190-193 (tool_accuracy None -> 1.0), 195-204 (empty runs -> verification/retry 1.0), 218-222 (empty -> hallucination 0.0), 244-270 (run_benchmark/compare_to_baseline); ring semantics metrics.py:271-308; per-process/ephemeral note base_graph.py:3818-3827; loop guard main.py:422-423
findings.finding: compare_to_baseline() computes the 'current' side from the calling process's in-memory MetricsCollector ring (run_benchmark -> collector.by_agent(agent, 20)). With zero runs in that window (fresh process, restart, or the agent ran in a different worker), every no-data branch resolves to its benign default, so benchmark_score = 1.0 (weights sum to exactly 1.00) and the diff against any stored baseline can never flag a regression. 'No current data' is treated as 'perfect current behavior' rather than 'unknown'. Combined with the deliberate no-baseline fallback, all gate paths pass unless the checking process itself holds at least one recent run of the target agent AND the fractional drop exceeds the 10% threshold. The baseline/auto-rollback loops are leader-elected, so only one process's ring feeds them, and MetricsCollector is explicitly documented in-code as in-process-only and reset on restart.
findings.evidence: Live test test_run_benchmark_with_no_runs_uses_benign_defaults PASSED (direct proof of the all-perfect no-runs score); weights sum to 1.00 (config.py:1343-1368); ring = deque(maxlen=1000) + _index, per-process singleton (metrics.py:271-308, 656-660); base_graph.py:3818-3827 comment: 'in-process-only, ephemeral observability system (reset on restart, invisible across processes)'; main.py:422 guard skips agents with no in-process runs when creating baselines.
findings.production_impact: After a restart or on a worker that has not run the target agent, the regression gate provides no protection (always passes) even when a real fleet regression exists - protection is provisional on in-process history, not a durable guarantee. Fail-open only: it can never block wrongly, but it can silently allow a regressed deploy.
findings.confidence: High (code-path derivation + passing no-runs-defaults test + in-code ring semantics)
findings.recommendation: Distinguish 'no current runs' from 'perfect score' (return an explicit insufficient_data state that callers treat as neutral/skip rather than a pass), or compute the current window from durable agent_runs/AgentBenchmark history instead of the in-process ring.

findings.location: real-LLM eval suite is excluded by default and never invoked by any workflow
findings.line: pytest.ini:6-8 (markers slow; addopts = -m "not slow"); ci.yml:82-83 (default suite only); repo-wide grep of .github/workflows/ for slow|eval_runner|tests/evals -> 0 matches
findings.finding: The 11-task LLM eval suite (tests/evals/) is marked slow and excluded by default (pytest.ini addopts), and no workflow anywhere invokes '-m slow', the eval runner, or a scheduled eval job. The only CI-adjacent eval execution is the fast definition-validation tests inside the general 'pytest tests/' run (which pass) - the actual LLM-graded agent evaluations never execute automatically. Live run confirms the exclusion: 59 collected, 4 deselected (the @pytest.mark.slow TestAgentEvals class).
findings.evidence: pytest.ini read; grep across .github/workflows/ for 'slow|eval_runner|tests/evals|-m "not slow"|marker' -> 0 matches; ci.yml:82-83 runs python -m pytest tests/ -v --tb=short --timeout=120; eval_runner.py:6-16 documents manual invocation (USE_GROQ=true GROQ_API_KEY=... plus pytest -m slow); local run output '59 collected / 4 deselected / 55 selected'.
findings.production_impact: Drift in agent output quality is caught only by manual runs; a green CI does not mean evals pass. Agent prompt changes deploy through the regression gate but are never eval-gated by automation. Bounded (no runtime impact).
findings.recommendation: Add a scheduled (nightly) workflow running the slow eval suite or python -m tests.evals.eval_runner with the Groq key, initially report-only/non-blocking in the same posture as the existing tech-debt scan step (ci.yml:108-121).

findings.location: hallucination_rate objective uses only the self-declared reflection proxy; the independently verified citation_hallucinations signal is recorded but never consumed by any objective
findings.line: benchmark_manager.py:215-222 (hallucination_rate = fraction of runs with reflection_unsatisfied > 0); metrics.py:137-145 (citation_hallucinations field + rationale #443); base_graph.py:2908+ (verify_file_line_citations), 4170-4172 (recorded), 4356-4359 (mirrored to agent_runs); reflection default-satisfied path base_graph.py:2038-2042
findings.finding: The composite's hallucination term consumes only reflection_unsatisfied - the model's own subjective judgment of its tool output - while RunMetrics.citation_hallucinations (a per-claim, code-checked signal from #443's verify_file_line_citations: cited file:line/function/class actually existing in the repo) is recorded into RunMetrics and the durable agent_runs row but read by no benchmark objective. The reflection proxy also under-counts when the reflection call fails to parse (defaults to satisfied=True) and unavoidably conflates 'missed edge cases' with factual hallucination.
findings.evidence: benchmark_manager.py:215-222 with its own in-code label 'Approximation, not ground truth'; grep shows zero uses of citation_hallucinations in fleet/benchmark_manager.py; the field is populated (base_graph.py:4170-4172) and persisted (finish_agent_run_sync call at 4356-4359).
findings.production_impact: The objective overestimates hallucination-freedom exactly in the cases where the model is least reliable at self-reporting; the 0.15 hallucination weight is the most proxy-dependent term of benchmark_score. Advisory improvement, not a runtime defect.
findings.recommendation: Add citation_hallucinations to the composite or as its own objective (e.g. rate of runs with failed citation verification, or per-claim failure rate) once real baseline volume exists; keep the reflection signal as a secondary input.
